steps.title: Global middleware, then /api/v1 mount
steps.caption: The request has no body, only the header "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>". The global urlencoded, json and cors middleware run first and do nothing useful here (req.body stays {}). Express strips /api/v1 and passes /users/handshake to the module router, which tries userRoutes first.

steps.title: Route matched
steps.caption: POST /users/handshake runs authenticate, then UserController.handshake. There is no validate() step: the route reads nothing from the body or URL, and the user id comes only from the login token.

steps.title: Bearer token read from header
steps.caption: "Bearer <jwt>" is split into the scheme "Bearer" and the token. A missing header or any other scheme stops the request here.

branches.when: no Authorization header, or scheme is not "Bearer"

steps.title: Login token verified, user attached
steps.caption: JWTService.verify checks the HS256 signature with ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET and the expiry (jsonwebtoken does this), then checks the payload shape with AccessTokenPayloadSchema. The token belongs to user 42, so req.user = { id: 42, email: "ada@example.com" }.

branches.when: bad signature, expired or malformed token
token is valid but its payload has no positive integer id or valid email

steps.title: Controller takes id from token
steps.caption: The id is 42 from req.user, never from the URL or body, so a caller can only get their own MQTT credentials. Any error thrown below is caught and passed to next(), which sends it to the error handler.

steps.title: User 42 loaded from Postgres
steps.caption: BaseService.findById runs SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 42 LIMIT 1 (Drizzle). The row exists. The login token is stateless, so this is the only place a deleted account is noticed.

branches.when: no user with id 42 (account deleted after login)

steps.title: Active room memberships loaded
steps.caption: activeRoomIds(42) reads room_members where user_id = 42 and status = 'active'. Ada is an active member of rooms 7 and 12; rows with status 'left' are skipped.

steps.title: user:42 written to Redis
steps.caption: toPublic drops the password hash. The public fields plus rooms [7, 12] are saved as JSON under user:42 with no expiry, replacing the whole value. room-service reads this key to allow enter-room without Postgres. A join that commits between s7 and this write is lost from the copy. Joining again or a new handshake repairs it.

steps.title: MQTT client id built
steps.caption: User 42 becomes the MQTT client id "user-42". ClientId is the only place that knows this format. Later, room-service turns "user-42" back into 42.

steps.title: Session token signed
steps.caption: signSession("user-42") signs an HS256 JWT with MQTT_TOKEN_SECRET: sub "user-42", aud "mqtt-session", a random jti, and an expiry of MQTT_TOKEN_EXPIRY seconds. It is not stored anywhere. Older tokens stay valid until they expire.

steps.title: Credentials assembled
steps.caption: The client id doubles as the MQTT username, and the session token is the MQTT password.

steps.title: 200 with MQTT credentials
steps.caption: Sends 200 { success: true, data: { clientId, mqttUsername, mqttPassword } }. The client then connects to the broker with these. The broker's login check (/auth/mqtt/user) currently answers "allow" to everyone; the password is really checked on every command by room-service's CommandGuard.

steps.title: 401: no Bearer token
steps.caption: No header, or something like "Basic ...", returns 401 { success: false, message: "Missing access token", status: 401 } from the error handler. The controller never runs.

steps.anchor: throw new Unauthorized("Invalid or expired token");
steps.title: 401: token invalid or expired
steps.caption: A tampered, expired or garbled token returns 401 "Invalid or expired token". The message doesn't say which, on purpose. An MQTT session token also fails here because it is signed with a different secret.

steps.anchor: throw new Unauthorized("Invalid or expired token");
steps.title: 401: payload has wrong shape
steps.caption: A correctly signed token whose payload lacks a positive integer id or a valid email gets the same 401 "Invalid or expired token".

steps.title: 403: account no longer exists
steps.caption: If user 42 was deleted while their login token is still valid, the response is 403 "User not found" (not 401 or 404). Nothing is written to Redis and no MQTT token is issued.

steps.title: 500: Postgres or Redis failure
steps.caption: A database or Redis error is not an AppError, so the error handler logs it and returns 500 "Internal Server Error". No token is issued, because signing happens only after the Redis write.
